question: What can a precisely specified computation accomplish?
idea: Some mathematical questions concern whether a procedure exists at all; others concern how much time or how accurate an approximation it needs. Those are different limits. This entry studies the particular computational question stated below.
why: The mathematics of computation: what algorithms can do, how much work they need, and which problems are hard to solve.

glossary.meaning: A precisely specified procedure for solving a problem or carrying out a computation.
The mathematics of uncertainty and random behavior.
A bound or statement whose control does not deteriorate across the specified range of inputs.

exactClaim: Gives a uniform randomized classical algorithm for worst-case Subset Sum in ordinary $O(2^{0.49n})$ word-RAM time on polynomial-bit inputs, where n counts the integers. The time bound holds on every execution and success probability is at least 2/3 on every input. Inputs may repeat positive integers; words have $O(n+b)$ bits for maximum input bit length b.
scope: A definition-led reading guide; the exact mathematical claim is preserved separately. This is not a proof assessment.
